invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).

Every save control a page offers makes exactly the same checks on that page's answers, with no page an exception: a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one and what they entered still shown, and the controls differ only in where they go once every answer passes (ruling:sam-2026-10-26).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: An empty species panel is refused on its own save, even beside a filled one
increments.detail: One identifier is enough to save a live animal, but an animal with no identifier at all is not a record. Today 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal' fires only when nothing is typed anywhere on the page, so with two species an empty panel's save is skipped silently while the other's data is there. The check moves to each panel: a panel save with every identifier of its current animal blank is refused on that panel. The page's own 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' still never block on missing identifiers, and the page still shows no message about the submit rule.
acceptanceCriteria: With cattle and dogs on the page, an ear tag typed into the cattle panel and nothing typed into the dog panel, pressing the dog panel's 'Save and add another' saves nothing and shows 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal' in the 'There is a problem' summary and inline on the dog panel's first identifier field; the summary link focuses that field. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-027; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-019; conflicts:c-042)

Pressing 'Save and finish' on a species' last animal still to enter, with every identifier of that animal blank, is refused the same way and the animal stays to enter. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-027; conflicts:c-042)
A partly filled animal, with one identifier given and the rest blank, saves with no error and is listed in that panel's saved-animals table. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-019; conflicts:c-042)

Pressing the page's 'Save and continue' or 'Save and return to overview' with every identifier blank saves no animal, shows no error and takes the trader on. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-028; conflicts:c-042)
notes: Unchanged in substance by this re-distil; criteria 3 and 4 were added so the row states the whole of req-234 as it stands, including the halves that must keep working.

increments.title: Identification counts as complete only when every animal is entered, and submit needs one entry per species when several are selected
increments.detail: Today the hub's Identification details row shows Complete straight after Commodity details, before any animal is identified, and stays Complete at 1 of 2. DR2.1 counts identification complete only when every animal of every selected species with identifier fields has a complete entry. For submitting, DR2.1 makes identification optional for a single species but needs at least one complete entry per species when more than one species is selected; the identification page itself shows no message for that rule.
acceptanceCriteria: Straight after Commodity details, with no animals entered, the hub's Identification details row does not show Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p6-002; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p10-003-m1)

With 1 of 2 cattle entered, the row does not show Complete; once both are entered with ear tag and passport it shows Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068; trace:e2e trace-e2e-p6-066)
A selected species with identifier fields but no number of animals keeps the row from showing Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-068)
With one species selected and no identification entered, the notification can be submitted. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070)

With two species with identifier fields selected and one of them without any complete entry, submitting is refused; once each has at least one complete entry, submitting goes ahead. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070; document:dr1-parity-backlog document-dr1-parity-backlog-p5-020)
The identification page shows no message about the submit rule. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-070)
notes: Combines the hub completion rule and the submit rule: both read the same 'complete entry' definition from the every-identifier row and change the same obligation evaluation. The submit refusal's place and wording belong to the review-and-submit area, which owns the submit gate and its messages (req-animal-identification-056's why); the criterion asserts only that submitting is refused or goes ahead. If that area drafts a row for the same gate, the combiner should merge this submit criterion into it or set dependsOn. The germinal half of the completion rule (a germinal species counts once its entry is saved) is proved in the germinal panel row. Builds after the every-identifier row in this area.

Dropped: req-248 and req-249 are adopted as already met. ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claims 13, 36 and 37 split off their germinal halves and settle that one identifier is enough for Complete and for submit, which the live-animals code does today; the germinal bar is req-261 in inc-183.

increments.title: Pigs, sheep and goats are identified by ear tag only
increments.detail: Pigs (0103), sheep (010410) and goats (010420) are identified per animal by 'Ear tag' only. The live-animal catalogue reaches the service from master data management, and the commodity integration that brings these three in is not this programme's to build, so the row waits for it. Once they are offered, each selected pig, sheep or goat species gets a panel asking for one ear tag per animal.
acceptanceCriteria: A selected pig species (0103) gets a panel asking for 'Ear tag' and no other identifier, once per animal. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-017)
A selected sheep (010410) or goat (010420) species gets a panel asking for 'Ear tag' and no other identifier, once per animal. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-021)

A pig, sheep or goat saved with an ear tag is listed in its saved-animals table, which has an 'Animal' column, an 'Ear tag' column and a 'Remove' action. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-017, prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-021)

Which identifier fields a species panel asks for follows the species rather than the commodity code alone: on commodity code 0101 a horse panel asks for a horse name, while a donkey, pony, zebra, mule or hinny panel asks only for the identifiers that species takes. (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p4-014, -p4-014-m1, -p4-043, -p4-106-m1; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p5-013; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-010)

increments.title: Cattle and pigs are asked for a tattoo, as V4's tattoo commodity list says
increments.detail: V4's 'Tattoo identifier commodities' list names 01061900 (cats, dogs and ferrets), 0103 (pigs) and 0102 (bovine), but the frontend offers a tattoo on 01061900 alone: TATTOO_CODES derives from COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS, which lists animalIdentifierTattoo under 01061900 only. A cattle panel gains a tattoo field after its ear tag and passport, and a pig panel gains one beside its ear tag. This reverses frontend commit b1ff013c, which removed the tattoo from cattle under DR1 parity on the grounds that DR1 asks a cow only for an ear tag and a passport; ruling:ian-2026-11-11 settles that V4 outranks every DR1 judgement, so V4's list is built and the parity change goes. The tattoo is placed last on cattle because that is where Design Release 2.1 puts it on the species that already ask for one.
acceptanceCriteria: A cattle (0102) species panel on Identification details asks for 'Ear tag', 'Passport' and 'Tattoo', in that order, and an animal saved with a tattoo alone saves with no error and is listed in that panel's saved-animals table with its tattoo shown (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p4-016, confluence-6497338582-p4-017, confluence-6497338582-p4-024, confluence-6497338582-p4-025; ruling:ian-2026-11-11; c-334)

A pig (0103) species panel asks for 'Ear tag' and 'Tattoo', and an animal saved with either one alone saves with no error (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p4-024, confluence-6497338582-p4-025, confluence-6497338582-p4-106; ruling:ian-2026-11-11; c-334)

A cattle animal's saved-animals table has an 'Animal' column and one column per identifier the species asks for, the tattoo column included, with a 'Remove' action on each row (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p4-105)

A tattoo of 59 characters is refused with 'Tattoo must be 58 characters or less' in the error summary and inline on the field, and one of 58 characters saves, on cattle and pigs as it already does on cats, dogs and ferrets (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-102)

The review page reads a cattle or pig animal's tattoo back in that species' identifier columns, as it already does for cats, dogs and ferrets (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-102; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p10-028)
A horse (0101) panel is not asked for a tattoo, and neither is any species V4's tattoo list does not name (confluence:6497338582 confluence-6497338582-p4-024)
The page's Welsh copy holds an entry for exactly the keys its English copy holds, and stays a machine draft (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-100)

increments.title: A permanent address page for cats, dogs and ferrets, with one card per animal and a same-as-destination choice
increments.detail: Each pet's permanent address is asked on its own page in the consignment parties section, opened from the consignment addresses page, instead of inside the animal identification form. Cats, dogs and ferrets need one. Other live mammals that share commodity code 01061900 do not. The page has a card for each animal that needs one, showing the identifiers already given, and asks for each whether the animal lives at the place of destination or at a new address, revealing the address fields only when a new address is chosen. Each animal's choice and address are stored with the notification, every field in its own place, and a trader can save what they know and come back.
acceptanceCriteria: A consignment with cats, dogs or ferrets has a 'Permanent address' section on the consignment addresses page explaining 'A permanent address is where an animal:' with the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' to the permanent address page; a consignment of cats alone has five sections and no county parish holding section (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-023, p9-025; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-085, p7-106; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-081; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p2-014, p2-015)

A consignment of cattle, horses or another 01061900 species, such as 'Carnivora excluding Canis familiaris, Felis catus, Mustela putorius furio', has a consignment addresses page with no permanent address section, and opening the permanent address page for it sends the trader to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-023, p9-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-109; document:dr1-parity-backlog p6-012, p6-015; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm p2-014, p2-015)

The permanent address page has the caption 'Consignment parties', the heading 'Permanent address', the browser title 'Permanent address - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and a back link to the consignment addresses page (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-021, p9-032, p9-033; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-109, p13-110; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-082, p3-108)
The animal identification page asks only for each animal's identifiers, and its species card ends with the identifier fields (document:dr1-parity-backlog p6-058; trace:e2e p6-028)

The page shows one card for each animal that needs a permanent address, as many as were entered for each species, headed with the scientific name and a running number such as 'Felis catus 1'; a ferret gets a card, and another 01061900 species on the same consignment gets none (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-037, p9-038; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-091, p13-111; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-084)

Each card shows the animal's entered identifiers in inset text as 'label: value', such as 'Microchip: MICROCHIP-1', leaving out blank ones, and shows no inset when none are entered (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-039; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-111)

Each card asks 'Select an address' with the options 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' and 'Enter a new address', neither chosen when the page first opens; once a place of destination is given, the first option's hint is that address on one line, such as 'Riverside Holding Facility, East Farm Road, Leeds, LS25 3EB, United Kingdom' (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-040, p9-041, p9-042; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-092, p7-094, p7-095, p13-112; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-085)

'Enter a new address' has the hint 'This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.', and choosing it reveals that animal's own address fields inside its card, with 'Email address' before 'Phone number' (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-042, p9-043, p9-050, p9-051; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-093, p7-097, p7-098, p13-113; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-086, p3-090)

Outside an amendment the page ends with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone, which saves and returns to the consignment addresses page (document:dr1-parity-notes p1-055, p1-056, p1-058; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-104; prototype:dr2-1-source p9-077)

An animal saved as 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' has the place of destination's name, address, country, email and phone as its permanent address on the review page, and reopening the permanent address page shows that option selected (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-067, p9-068; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p13-115; prototype:dr2-1-specs p4-039)

A new address saved with a county and no address line 2 reopens with 'Enter a new address' selected, each value in its own field: the county in 'County', the town in 'Town or city' and the postcode in 'Postcode or Zip code', with country United Kingdom (ruling:sam-2026-10-07 p1-010; prototype:dr2-1-source p9-068; trace:e2e p6-032)

An animal left with no option chosen is saved with no permanent address: the page saves the other animals and returns to the consignment addresses page, the permanent address section there reads as incomplete, and the notification cannot be submitted until every animal that needs one has an address with a name (prototype:dr2-1-source p9-062, p9-063, p9-074; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p7-102; prototype:dr2-1-specs p3-089)

With the Welsh language chosen, every new string on the permanent address page and the addresses page's permanent address section shows in Welsh, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off (repo:frontend p10-050, p10-083)

openQuestions: For the designer: on the permanent address page the over-long address messages name three fields differently from those fields own labels and own blank messages, and differently again from the same form elsewhere in the service. The code takes them from the owning party-edit copy through address-rules.js: frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-edit/copy/copy.en.js:23, :41, :48 give "Name must be 255 characters or fewer", "Postcode must be 12 characters or fewer", "Telephone number must be 20 characters or fewer" (read at frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/permanent-address/save-rules.js:35). This page labels the same fields "Name or organisation name", "Postcode or Zip code" and "Phone number" (frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/permanent-address/copy/copy.en.js:13, :18, :20) and words its blank messages the same long way (:26, :29, :31). The service other address form already words the over-long message the long way: frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:238, :243, :247 give "Name or organisation name must be 255 characters or less", "Postcode or Zip code must be 12 characters or less", "Phone number must be 20 characters or less". The design source sets no over-long message at all - prototype:dr2-1-specs consignment-parties.fit.spec.js:334-341 proves only the six blank messages - and ruling:ian-2026-11-11 (this row notes) sets only the sentence shape "<field> must be N characters or fewer", leaving which name fills <field> to the implementation. GDS error-message guidance says an error message should name the field as its label does: https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-message/. Options: (a) name the field as its label does, on this page and on party-edit - "Name or organisation name must be 255 characters or fewer", "Postcode or Zip code must be 12 characters or fewer", "Phone number must be 20 characters or fewer"; or (b) keep the party-edit wording "Name / Postcode / Telephone number must be N characters or fewer" on both pages. Whichever is chosen is the one wording for every address form in the service, and "or fewer" against the transporter form "or less" is settled with it. Raised by review finding 9 on inc-055.

For the designer: the permanent address page empty-state copy is shown for a sub-state the design source does not cover - a trader who has already given the number of animals is still told to add it. In this service a card comes from an animal identifier record, not from the line animal count (frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/permanent-address/cards.js:44-55 keys cards off animalIdentifiers; frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/page-design.md says cards come from the records entered, never from the line animal count), so the empty state is reachable with a count already given, and the code shows "Add the number of animals on consignment details before you can continue." (frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/permanent-address/copy/copy.en.js:36-40) pointing at a page the trader has already answered. This change own feature test reaches exactly that state - frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/permanent-address/permanent-address.fit.spec.js:507-510 fills the number of animals with 1 and then expects the message. In the design source the cards come from the count: the prototype keys one radio group per counted animal (prototype:dr2-1-specs consignment-parties.fit.spec.js:301, :313, :323 give permanentAddressChoice[cat-felis-catus:0] and :1 for a count of 2), so its empty state only arises with no count at all, which is what criterion 5 says ("With no animals that need a permanent address counted"). Options: (a) one message covers both sub-states, as built now; or (b) a count given with no identifier record gets its own words pointing at the animal identification page, for example "Identify the animals on <link>animal identification</link> before you can continue.", keeping "Add the number of animals on consignment details before you can continue." only for a line with no count at all. Raised by review finding 11 on inc-055; the plan records it as a section 7 follow-up but builds one message for both sub-states.

Scope check against ruling:ian-2026-11-11, which found one thing to carry into the plan. V4 specifies the Standard Address Block authoritatively (confluence-6497338582-p6-005 to p6-052) and says Permanent Address is that block with that block's field-level validation (p2-047, p2-052, which this theme cites). So the address limits are V4's, not this page's to invent: name and both address lines 255 characters, town or city and county 100, postcode 12, telephone 20, email 254, and p6-052 records that V4's Validation column states no format rule, pattern or permitted-character set for any address field. increments.title: Pressing Enter in a species panel saves that panel's own animal and reaches no other panel's buttons
increments.detail: Today one hidden 'Save and finish' submit button sits at the top of the whole form and is the default submit for every field on the page, whichever species panel the field belongs to. With a panel per species, and a 'Remove' button on every saved animal, that single default submit is the wrong owner for a field: pressing Enter in a panel's field should save that panel's current animal, as the panel's own save button does, and it should never reach a 'Remove' action or another panel's save. The trader keeps every animal they have already saved and every value they have typed, and a keyboard or screen-reader user meets no button inside a panel that is not one of the panel's own.
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing Enter in a field of a species panel that takes more than one animal saves that panel's current animal, as that panel's own save button does, and leaves the trader on the page with the values they entered still shown. (ruling:sam-2026-10-26 ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-016, -p1-017, -p1-018, -p1-019, -p1-020; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-076; trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p10-081)

Pressing Enter in an identifier field of a species panel that already has saved animals leaves every one of those animals listed in that panel's saved-animals table, and leaves every other panel's saved animals listed too. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-076, repo-frontend-p6-090, repo-frontend-p6-091; ruling:sam-2026-10-26 ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-019)

The buttons a keyboard or screen-reader user reaches inside a species panel are that panel's own save button and a 'Remove' action for each animal it has saved; tabbing forward from the panel's last identifier field reaches one of those next. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p6-067, repo-frontend-p6-068, repo-frontend-p6-076, repo-frontend-p6-090)

openQuestions: Main saves every card holding a typed value when Enter is pressed (EUDPA-734's own commit message: 'Enter saves every card holding a typed value'), while criterion 1 says Enter in a panel saves 'that panel's current animal, as that panel's own save button does'. The two are compatible wherever only one panel has been typed into, so no criterion fails today, but they are different designs once two panels hold typed values. Confirm which is wanted before writing the keyboard walk, because the walk's assertions differ.
notes: New row this re-distil: req-205 sat in no row before. A thin slice of its own, kept apart from the fallback-panel row: it needs a panel with saved animals and a keyboard walk, not a new commodity line, so the two share no set-up.

This row covers only what the default submit must never do. The other half of the keyboard behaviour, that pressing Enter in a panel for several animals saves that panel's current animal and keeps what the trader typed, is already a row on the design snagging follow-ups branch (inc-224, from ruling:sam-2026-10-26 claims 17 to 19), so it is deliberately left out here to avoid building it twice. Build this row's criteria as tests against whatever that branch has landed, and change code only where a test fails.
